Your first speaking session: how to start without an audience

Your first speaking session does not need an audience or a correction. A few known words and your voice are enough. Here is how to start alone, tonight.

Published April 12, 2024 · 7 min read · Sławomir Onyszko ·Updated November 14, 2026

You have whole sentences in your head. You know how to say that it is raining, that you were late for work, that you like coffee with milk. Then someone asks you a simple question, and your mind goes blank.

Instead of speaking, you do something safer. You finish another course, learn more words, or look for a patient person who will not judge you. The wait can last years, because every time it feels like one more thing is missing.

Speaking is not an exam you pass once you know enough. It is a skill you build by doing it. You do not need an audience or a perfect accent. For the first session, a few words you already know and your voice are enough.

Why waiting feels safer than speaking

When you read or listen, you stay in control. You recognize words and understand the meaning. Nothing embarrassing happens. When you speak, you hear your own voice and your own mistakes, even when nobody is listening. That feeling is awkward, so it is easier to put speaking off.

Recognition and speaking are different skills. You can understand a sentence when someone else says it and still freeze when you have to build it. Reading about swimming will not teach you to swim until you get in the water.

I know this feeling. For years I understood more than I could say. The first time I recorded myself, I was alone in my room. It was awkward, but it was the first time I heard the gap between what I knew and what I could say.

Vocabulary is the base, but it is not enough

Words are the building blocks. Without words, you cannot build a sentence. But a list of words you only recognize does not turn into speaking. A word becomes yours when you use it in your own sentence.

You do not need a huge list for the first session. 3 to 5 words you already know but rarely use in speech are enough. For example: casa, trabajo, comer, ir, gustar. You can take them from a list of common words or from your own day.

This is the difference between passive and active vocabulary. Passive vocabulary is made of words you recognize but do not reach for when you speak. Active vocabulary is what you actually use. Speaking turns one into the other.

The first session does not need a correction

That sounds strange, because good practice is built on corrections. But the first session is different. It is a check that you can say your own sentence out loud. You do not have to fix mistakes right away. You have to hear what you have.

The first session looks like this:

  1. Pick 3 to 5 words you know. Choose words you rarely use in speech, but whose meaning you know.
  2. Build 3 sentences about yourself or your day. Simple sentences are fine.
  3. Say them out loud. Do not read from a card. Do not correct yourself while you speak.
  4. Record yourself. You can use your phone, a voice recorder, or an app.
  5. Play the recording and listen once, without stopping.
  6. Save one word you were missing as a flashcard. Not all of them, just one.

That is all. No story, no tutor, no correction. A story can come later, but it is not a requirement. The first session takes 5 minutes, not 15. The 15-minute session comes later, when correction and review join in.

You do not have to wait for a session at a desk. You can talk to yourself during the day: making coffee, walking to the bus, closing your laptop. Every sentence out loud is a small practice.

What you hear in the recording

When you play the recording, you will hear three things:

  • where you stopped
  • which word was missing
  • what sounded different from what you meant

These are not corrections. They are observations. They show you what to work on next. If you stopped at "trabajo", that word comes back as a flashcard. If the sentence sounded stiff, maybe a simple connector was missing. You do not have to fix it right away.

What this session will not do

This session will not fix your grammar. It will not give you a specific correction. It will not make you fluent tomorrow. Those are not flaws, they are the limits of the first step.

But that does not mean correction is unnecessary. The opposite is true. Correction is the next step, and without it, practice can repeat the same mistake. The first session shows you what you have. Correction shows you what to do with it.

Where the correction comes from

You have three options.

A tutor. Conversation with a tutor is the best way to practice real conversation. A tutor can interrupt, ask a question, and react to what you say. You have to book a time, so a tutor is not always at hand.

Language exchange. Someone who is learning your language while you learn theirs. You can correct each other. It is good when you want to talk to a person, but you do not always get a specific correction.

An app that asks you to build your own sentence and shows you a corrected version. It works every day without booking. It will not replace real conversation, but it gives you a correction when you want to practice.

Soliloquy puts this in one path: a lexicon of the most common words, flashcards where you try to remember before you look, spaced review, and speaking practice that activates the words. Stories are an optional extra, not a requirement.

What to do when you freeze

When you freeze, lower the difficulty. Describe what you see in the room. Say 3 sentences about your day. Use words you know, even if the grammar is rough. A short, imperfect answer is better than a perfect answer you never record.

If you have no words, describe the thing around the missing word. "The thing you use to cut bread" is a useful answer if you do not know "cuchillo". The correction will give you the word later. That is how the gap gets smaller.

A first week without a tutor

  • Day 1: Pick 3 words, build 3 sentences, record, listen. Save one missing word.
  • Day 2: Review the flashcard from day 1. Say the sentence with that word out loud.
  • Day 3: Pick 3 new words. Build 3 sentences about yesterday.
  • Day 4: Listen to the recordings from days 1 and 3. Notice one difference.
  • Day 5: Ask for one correction. A tutor, language exchange, or an app.
  • Day 6: Say the corrected sentence out loud 3 times.
  • Day 7: Record a new version with the corrected sentence. Save one new word.

If you miss a day, continue the next day. The plan is only a suggestion, not a streak you have to protect.

Hard questions

Do I need a tutor to start?

No. For the first recording, you do not need a tutor. Conversation with a tutor is the best way to practice real conversation and get corrections, but it is not a condition for the first step.

What if I make mistakes?

Mistakes are the material. The first session is there to hear them, not to fix them right away. The correction comes later.

How long should a session take?

The first session is 5 minutes. When correction and review join in, 10 to 15 minutes is enough.

What if I do not know enough words?

Use the words you know and describe the thing around the missing one. Save the missing word as a flashcard. The correction will give you the rest.

Start with 3 sentences

Tonight, pick 3 words you know. Build 3 sentences about your day. Say them out loud and record yourself. Play the recording once. That is the whole first session.

If you want correction and review in one place, Soliloquy takes you through the lexicon, flashcards, and speaking. But the first 3 sentences you can say tonight without an app and without an audience.
